title: Paloma and the Autopsy
premise: When a drowned man washes up in the cathedral crypt wearing clothes cut from Emrys Okafor's own wardrobe, the quiet archivist becomes both witness and suspect in a town that has spent fifteen years pretending not to see him. The dead man is connected to a fire nineteen years ago that killed three people, and Emrys's predecessor left behind a ledger disguised as a catalogue of saints' relics that names who paid for silence. As the trial of the town's beloved doctor approaches, Emrys must choose between protecting the found family that took him in and exposing the truth that will burn them all. In the end, he testifies, the ledger convicts the doctor's patron—the cathedral dean—and Emrys finally stops being invisible by becoming the man everyone watches.
about_author: W. M. Okafor is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing documents no one was meant to read. They write mysteries about archives, small towns, and the violence hidden in orderly places.

chapters.title: The Catalogue of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Emrys Okafor introduces his meticulously ordered life as cathedral archivist: alphabetized ledgers, a locked crypt, and a town that greets him without seeing him. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: Water in the Reliquary
chapters.summary: A maintenance worker finds a drowned man in the sealed crypt, dressed in a suit Emrys recognizes as his own—stitched from fabric missing from his closet for years. The police seal the archive. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: violation; his sanctuary has been used against him.

chapters.title: Detective Ibarra's Questions
chapters.summary: Detective Ibarra interviews Emrys, noting the clothes fit him perfectly and that the crypt key exists in only two copies. Emrys lies smoothly about the second key—an instinct honed by years of keeping secrets. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: A woman named Paloma Reyes claims she saw someone carrying the body toward the cathedral—but her description matches Emrys exactly. She is the town's unreliable drunk, yet her testimony sets the trial date. POV: alternating Emrys and Paloma. Emotional beat: dread of being seen wrongly.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Filing
chapters.summary: Emrys reviews what he knows: he inherited the archive from Father Anselm, who died mysteriously, and never questioned why the crypt stayed locked. He begins pulling records on the dead man, identified as Tomas Vidal. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: guilt over willful blindness.

chapters.title: Paloma Remembers Fire
chapters.summary: Paloma, sober for eleven days, recalls the night of the Aldgate House fire nineteen years ago—Tomas Vidal was a boy who survived it, like she did. She recognizes something in the corpse's hands. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing through sobriety.

chapters.title: Saints Who Never Lived
chapters.summary: Emrys discovers anomalies in Anselm's relic catalogue: entries for saints that don't exist, each with dates matching payments in the cathedral accounts. It's a cipher. Someone paid the church to bury the fire's cause. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the thrill of purpose after years of stasis.

chapters.title: The Doctor's Alibi
chapters.summary: Dr. Celeste Marchetti, the town's beloved physician and Emrys's only friend, is arrested for Vidal's murder. Her alibi is thin; her connection to Vidal unexplained. Emrys wants to believe her. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: loyalty colliding with doubt.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Buys
chapters.summary: Decoding further, Emrys finds the initials C.M. beside the largest payment—Celeste's name in the old ledger. Either she bought silence about the fire, or someone framed her twice, nineteen years apart. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: betrayal's cold arithmetic.

chapters.title: Paloma's Closet
chapters.summary: Emrys confronts Paloma and realizes the stolen clothes came from a donation bin outside her building—a bin Celeste's clinic empties weekly. The frame was built from proximity, not malice. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: two survivors recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Anselm's Last Entry
chapters.summary: In the deepest shelf, Emrys finds Anselm's final journal page: 'The Dean knows what burned. I cannot file this.' Father Anselm didn't die naturally—he was silenced. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: horror at how deep the rot goes.

chapters.title: Dean Wexler's Generosity
chapters.summary: Dean Wexler offers Emrys a promotion and a quiet transfer before the trial, framing it as protection. His kindness has the texture of a bribe. Emrys accepts the meeting but not the offer. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: temptation of continued invisibility.

chapters.title: The Night Visitor
chapters.summary: Someone ransacks the archive overnight, taking the relic catalogue. Emrys had photographed every page—he just hadn't told anyone. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: terror transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: Trial Opens
chapters.summary: Celeste's trial begins; the prosecution leans on Paloma's eyewitness account. On the stand, Paloma falters—her memory of the figure is real, but the face she described was suggested to her by an officer close to Wexler. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: courage costing everything.

chapters.title: Decoding the Saints
chapters.summary: Working from photographs, Emrys cracks the full cipher: the payments trace to Wexler, covering arson at Aldgate House—an insurance scheme that killed three people, including Vidal's parents. Celeste's signature was forged on one entry. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: clarity arriving too late to feel like victory.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Emrys brings the decoded ledger to Ibarra, who reveals she's suspected Wexler for months but needed the cipher to act. She warns him: witnesses against the Dean have short lifespans. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: choosing truth knowing its cost.

chapters.title: Locked In
chapters.summary: Wexler traps Emrys in the crypt with the second key—the one Anselm hid, which Wexler has held for fifteen years. He confesses to Anselm's death and Vidal's, offering Emrys the same deal: file it away and live. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the claustrophobia of a lifetime's habit of hiding.

chapters.title: Paloma at the Door
chapters.summary: Paloma, unable to sleep, comes to return a borrowed book and hears Emrys pounding beneath the floor. She fetches Ibarra, defying the officer loyal to Wexler who tries to stop her. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: the witness becoming the rescuer.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Emrys takes the stand instead of staying invisible, presenting the cipher, the forged signature, and Anselm's journal. Wexler's composure cracks under the dates he himself encoded. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: terror and liberation in the same breath.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Wexler is convicted; Celeste walks free, but the friendship is scarred—she can't forgive that Emrys doubted her. The town must reckon with what its beloved institutions buried. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: justice without warmth.

chapters.title: Reordering
chapters.summary: Emrys reopens the crypt as a memorial to the fire's victims, recataloguing Anselm's true legacy alongside the false saints. Paloma helps, sober, hired as the archive's first assistant. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: grief given structure, loneliness loosening.

chapters.title: Paloma and the Autopsy
chapters.summary: Months later, Paloma asks Emrys why he titled his new finding-aid after her. He answers that she was the first person to look at him and describe him accurately. The town still whispers, but he is, at last, seen. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted.
